results.content: Ali, M.M., Hamid, M.O. Governmental rationalities and misrecognising human and social conditions in English-in-education policy for individual and social development. • This article provides fresh perspectives in language policy research to critique development in relation to language-in-education policy (LEP) in developing countries. • LEP is a key tool for human capital development. • Sen’s conceptualisation of development is dominant in language policy/education research, but we find this idea problematic as Sen is complicit to human capital theory/ neoliberalism. • Ideological perspective is important to unpack the politics of development discourses and how these are used to govern populations in interested ways. • Misrecognition is central to governing neoliberal citizens and how unequal social struggles over linguistic human capital development are accepted as natural. results.content: Thematic analysis of the data reveals that while English-in-education policy creates neoliberal subjectivities among students and parents in relation to a transformative social imaginary and better economic futures, LEP misrecognises how the acquisition of the linguistic capital of English is conditioned by their human and social experiences of living. Our framework contributes to the social justice agenda in relation to language policy and education for human capital development by unpacking how misrecognition operates through governmental rationalities and dispositions shaped by development ideologies.
